urbex.preview.seed_locked: The preview follows the world seed you typed. Clear the Seed field to roll preview seeds.
urbex.preset.disabled.info: Urbex leaves this world alone: no cities, no ruins, no highways.
urbex.setting.DEBRIS_TO_NEARBYCHUNK_FACT: A factor that determines how much debris will overflow from nearby damaged chunks. Bigger numbers mean less debris
urbex.setting.VINE_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a block on the outside of a building will be covered with a vine
urbex.setting.CHANCE_OF_RANDOM_LEAFBLOCK: Chance that leafblocks will be generated at the border of a building and a street
urbex.setting.THICKNESS_OF_RANDOM_LEAFBL: Frequency of leafblocks as seen from the sides of buildings
urbex.setting.AVOID_FOLIAGE.tooltip: If this is true then parks will have no foliage (trees and flowers currently)
urbex.setting.SCATTERED_CHANCE_MULTIPLIE: Multiplier for the chance a scattered building will generate. With 0 all scattered buildings are disabled
urbex.setting.RUBBLELAYER.tooltip: If this is true an alternative way to generate dirt/stone/sand + leave blocks is used that makes the city appear more overgrown
urbex.setting.RUBBLE_DIRT_SCALE.tooltip: The scale of the dirt layer. Smaller values make the layer larger. Use 0 to disable
urbex.setting.RUBBLE_LEAVE_SCALE.tooltip: The scale of the leave layer. Smaller values make the layer larger. Use 0 to disable
urbex.setting.RUIN_CHANCE.tooltip: This gives the chance that a building is ruined
urbex.setting.RUIN_MINLEVEL_PERCENT.tool: If a building is ruined this indicates the minimum start height for the ruin destruction layer
urbex.setting.RUIN_MAXLEVEL_PERCENT.tool: If a building is ruined this indicates the maximum start height for the ruin destruction layer
urbex.setting.HIGHWAY_REQUIRES_TWO_CITIE: If true then a highway will only generate if both sides have a valid city. If false then one city is sufficient
urbex.setting.HIGHWAY_LEVEL_FROM_CITIES_: 0 (take height from top-left city), 1 (take minimum height from both cities), 2 (take maximum height from both cities), 3 (take average height)
urbex.setting.HIGHWAY_MAINPERLIN_SCALE.t: For highways on a certain axis, this value is used to scale the perlin noise generator on the main axis. Increasing this value will increase the frequency of highways but make them smaller
urbex.setting.HIGHWAY_SECONDARYPERLIN_SC: For highways on a certain axis, this value is used to scale the perlin noise generator on the secondary axis. Increasing this value will increase the variation of nearby highways
urbex.setting.HIGHWAY_PERLIN_FACTOR.tool: The highway perlin noise is compared to this value. Setting this to 0 would give 50% chance of a highway being at a spot. Note that highways only generate on chunks a multiple of 8. Setting this very high will prevent highways from generating
urbex.setting.HIGHWAY_DISTANCE_MASK.tool: Mask to control how far highways can generate. Must be a power of 2 (minus 1). If 0 there are no highways at all
urbex.setting.HIGHWAY_SUPPORTS.tooltip: If true highways get supports when needed. You can disable this if you have highways that span void chunks
urbex.setting.RAILWAY_DUNGEON_CHANCE.too: The chance that a chunk next to a railway will have a railway dungeon
urbex.setting.RAILWAYS_CAN_END.tooltip: If true the a place where a station would have been if there was a city above will have an 'ending' rail part if one side of the 'station' has no connections. Useful in case cities are rare
urbex.setting.RAILWAYS_ENABLED.tooltip: If true then railways are enabled. If false they are not (but stations will still generate)
urbex.setting.RAILWAY_STATIONS_ENABLED.t: If true then railway stations are enabled
urbex.setting.RAILWAY_SURFACE_STATIONS_E: If true then railway surface station are enabled, otherwise there'll only be underground stations.
If this is true the center of an explosion can only be in a city (the blast can still affect non-city chunks)
urbex.setting.GENERATE_NETHER.tooltip: If true then generate a cavern type world in the Nether
urbex.setting.GENERATE_SPAWNERS.tooltip: If true then the buildings will be full of spawners
urbex.setting.LIGHTING_DENSITY.tooltip: Chance that an optional decorative-light marker places a light
urbex.setting.LOOT_DENSITY.tooltip: Chance that a marked container receives a loot table
urbex.setting.AVOID_WATER.tooltip: If true then all water will be avoided (replaced with air)
urbex.setting.EXPLOSION_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a chunk will contain an explosion
urbex.setting.EXPLOSION_MINRADIUS.toolti: The minimum radius of an explosion
urbex.setting.EXPLOSION_MAXRADIUS.toolti: The maximum radius of an explosion
urbex.setting.EXPLOSION_MINHEIGHT.toolti: The minimum height of an explosion
urbex.setting.EXPLOSION_MAXHEIGHT.toolti: The maximum height of an explosion
urbex.setting.MINI_EXPLOSION_CHANCE.tool: The chance that a chunk will contain a mini explosion
urbex.setting.MINI_EXPLOSION_MINRADIUS.t: The minimum radius of a mini explosion
urbex.setting.MINI_EXPLOSION_MAXRADIUS.t: The maximum radius of a mini explosion
urbex.setting.MINI_EXPLOSION_MINHEIGHT.t: The minimum height of a mini explosion
urbex.setting.MINI_EXPLOSION_MAXHEIGHT.t: The maximum height of a mini explosion
urbex.setting.CITY_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance this chunk will be the center of a city (use -1 for perlin noise variant)
urbex.setting.CITY_MINRADIUS.tooltip: The minimum radius of a city
urbex.setting.CITY_MAXRADIUS.tooltip: The maximum radius of a city
urbex.setting.CITY_PERLIN_SCALE.tooltip: The scale for the city rarity perlin map
urbex.setting.CITY_PERLIN_INNERSCALE.too: The internal scale for the city rarity perlin map
urbex.setting.CITY_PERLIN_OFFSET.tooltip: The offset for the city rarity perlin map
urbex.setting.CITY_THRESHOLD.tooltip: The center and radius of a city define a sphere. This threshold indicates from which point a city is considered a city. This is important for calculating where cities are based on overlapping city circles (where the city thresholds are added)
urbex.setting.CITY_SPAWN_DISTANCE1.toolt: At this distance from spawn (in blocks) the city factor will be equal to CITY_SPAWN_MULTIPLIER1
urbex.setting.CITY_SPAWN_DISTANCE2.toolt: At this distance from spawn (in blocks) the city factor will be equal to CITY_SPAWN_MULTIPLIER2. If this is 0 then no scaling is done
urbex.setting.CITY_STYLE_THRESHOLD.toolt: A city factor below this threshold will use the city style specified in 'cityStyleAlternative'
urbex.setting.CITY_STYLE_ALTERNATIVE.too: Alternative city style. Used with cityStyleThreshold
urbex.setting.CITY_AVOID_VOID.tooltip: Only used with floating landscape type: if true an additional detection is done to see if the chunk is void and in that case the city isn't generated there. Otherwise you might get city chunks on the border of islands which sometimes looks weird
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_32GRID.tooltip: If this is true then city spheres are aligned to a 32x32 grid. Otherwise they are aligned to a 16x16 grid
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_FACTOR.tooltip: Only used in 'space' landscape. This factor will be multiplied with the radius of the city to calculate the radius of the outer sphere
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a city sphere will be generated
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_SURFACE_VARIATI: Smaller numbers make the surface inside a city sphere more varied
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_OUTSIDE_SURFACE: Smaller numbers make the surface outside a city sphere more varied
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_MONORAIL_CHANCE: The chance that a city will have a monorail connection in a certain direction. There will only be an actual connection if there is a city in that direction that also wants a monorail
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_CLEARABOVE.tool: Number of blocks to clear above the top city sphere glass (0 is disabled)
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_CLEARBELOW.tool: Number of blocks to clear below the top city sphere (0 is disabled)
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_CLEARABOVE_UNTI: If enabled this will additionally clear blocks above what is already cleared by CLEARBOVE until air is reached
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_CLEARBELOW_UNTI: If enabled this will additionally clear blocks below what is already cleared by CLEARBELOW until air is reached
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_OUTSIDE_GROUNDL: Ground level for outside city spheres (DEPRECATED, USE GROUNDLEVEL OF OTHER PROFILE)
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_OUTSIDE_PROFILE: An optional profile to use for the outside world
urbex.setting.CITYSPHERE_ONLY_PREDEFINED: If this is true then only predefined spheres are generated
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL0_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 0
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL1_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 1
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL2_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 2
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL3_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 3
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL4_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 4
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL5_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 5
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL6_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 6
urbex.setting.CITY_LEVEL7_HEIGHT.tooltip: Below this chunk height cities will be level 7
urbex.setting.CITY_MINHEIGHT.tooltip: Below this height cities will not be generated
urbex.setting.CITY_MAXHEIGHT.tooltip: Above this height cities will not be generated
urbex.setting.OCEAN_CORRECTION_BORDER.to: Terrain correction offset that is used for chunks adjacent to city chunks that are in ocean biomes
urbex.setting.TERRAIN_FIX_LOWER_MIN_OFFS: To fix terrain adjacent to cities, this is the minimum offset (relative to city base level) for the lower mesh used to potentially raise the terrain
urbex.setting.TERRAIN_FIX_LOWER_MAX_OFFS: To fix terrain adjacent to cities, this is the maximum offset (relative to city base level) for the lower mesh used to potentially raise the terrain
urbex.setting.TERRAIN_FIX_UPPER_MIN_OFFS: To fix terrain adjacent to cities, this is the minimum offset (relative to city base level) for the upper mesh used to potentially lower the terrain
urbex.setting.TERRAIN_FIX_UPPER_MAX_OFFS: To fix terrain adjacent to cities, this is the maximum offset (relative to city base level) for the upper mesh used to potentially lower the terrain
urbex.setting.BUILDING_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a chunk in a city will have a building. Otherwise it will be a street
urbex.setting.BUILDING_MINFLOORS.tooltip: The minimum number of floors (above ground) for a building (0 means the first floor only)
urbex.setting.BUILDING_MAXFLOORS.tooltip: A cap for the amount of floors a city can have (above ground)
The amount of floors of a building is equal to: MINFLOORS + random(MINFLOORS_CHANCE + (cityFactor + .1f) * (MAXFLOORS_CHANCE - MINFLOORS_CHANCE))
The amount of floors of a building is equal to: MINFLOORS + random(MINFLOORS_CHANCE + (cityFactor + .1f) * (MAXFLOORS_CHANCE - MINFLOORS_CHANCE))
urbex.setting.BUILDING_MINCELLARS.toolti: The minimum number of cellars (below ground). 0 means no cellar
urbex.setting.BUILDING_MAXCELLARS.toolti: The maximum number of cellars (below ground). 0 means no cellar
urbex.setting.BUILDING_DOORWAYCHANCE.too: The chance that a doorway will be generated at a side of a building (on any level). Only when possible
urbex.setting.BUILDING_FRONTCHANCE.toolt: The chance that a building will have a 'front' part if this is possible (i.e. adjacent street)
urbex.setting.PARK_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a non-building section can be a park section
urbex.setting.CORRIDOR_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a chunk can possibly contain a corridor. There actually being a corridor also depends on the presence of adjacent corridors
urbex.setting.BRIDGE_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a chunk can possibly contain a bridge. There actually being a bridge also depends on the presence of adjacent bridges and other conditions
urbex.setting.FOUNTAIN_CHANCE.tooltip: The chance that a street section contains a fountain
urbex.setting.BRIDGE_SUPPORTS.tooltip: If true bridges get supports when needed. You can disable this if you have bridges that span void chunks
urbex.setting.PARK_ELEVATION.tooltip: If true parks get an extra layer of elevation
urbex.setting.PARK_BORDER.tooltip: If true parks border will use the street block as base.
urbex.setting.PARK_STREET_THRESHOLD.tool: Determines how many surrounding street it needs to generate a park, based on current chunk's park chance.
urbex.setting.MULTI_USE_CORNER.tooltip: Determine whether the multibuilding should use surrounding average level, or just top left corner level.
urbex.setting.USE_AVG_HEIGHTMAP.tooltip: City normal level generation is now dependent on surrounding heightmap and get an average of the surrounding heightmap. This uses extra performance since it needs to retrieve surrounding city heightmaps.
urbex.setting.BEDROCK_LAYER.tooltip: The height of the bedrock layer that is generated at the bottom of some world types. Set to 0 to disable this and get default bedrock generation
urbex.setting.HORIZON.tooltip: This is used client-side (but only if the client has this mod) to set the height of the horizon
urbex.setting.FOG_RED.tooltip: This is used client-side (but only if the client has this mod) for the fog color
urbex.setting.FOG_GREEN.tooltip: This is used client-side (but only if the client has this mod) for the fog color
urbex.setting.FOG_BLUE.tooltip: This is used client-side (but only if the client has this mod) for the fog color
urbex.setting.FOG_DENSITY.tooltip: This is used client-side (but only if the client has this mod) for the fog density
urbex.setting.SPAWN_BIOME.tooltip: When this is set the player will always spawn in the given biome
urbex.setting.SPAWN_CITY.tooltip: When this is set the player will always spawn in the given predefined city
urbex.setting.SPAWN_SPHERE.tooltip: When this is set the player will always spawn in the given predefined sphere. If you use <in> the player will always spawn in a random sphere. If you use <out> the player will always spawn outside a sphere
urbex.setting.SPAWN_NOT_IN_BUILDING.tool: If this is true the player will not spawn in a building. This can be used in combination with the other spawn settings
urbex.setting.FORCE_SPAWN_IN_BUILDING.to: If this is true the player will spawn in a building. This can be used in combination with the other spawn settings
urbex.setting.FORCE_SPAWN_BUILDINGS.tool: A list of buildings that the player will spawn in if FORCE_SPAWN_IN_BUILDING is true. If this is empty then any building will do. This can be used in combination with 'forceSpawnParts'
urbex.setting.FORCE_SPAWN_PARTS.tooltip: A list of parts that the player will spawn in if FORCE_SPAWN_IN_BUILDING is true. If this is empty then any part will do. This can be used in combination with 'forceSpawnBuildings'
urbex.setting.SPAWN_CHECK_RADIUS.tooltip: The start radius to check for a valid spawn location. This value will be increased with 100 if it couldn't find a valid spot
urbex.setting.SPAWN_RADIUS_INCREASE.tool: The radius increase to use if the spawn check radius is not large enough to find a valid spawn location
urbex.setting.SPAWN_CHECK_ATTEMPTS.toolt: The number of attempts to find a valid spawn location. If this is not enough then this will error
